events.what: Jerby preprint claims, assuming RH, that zeros of Hardy's Z-function obey the GUE pair-correlation law (Theorem C)
events.credibility_reason: Several F5 signals together: a full-range pair correlation result, even under RH, would be a landmark far beyond known methods; ten months with no citation, no MathOverflow or blog discussion; same-topic silence, since the live Wikipedia article covers adjacent 2025 work (Goldston–Lee–Schettler–Suriajaya) but not this, and those groups keep treating PCC as a hypothesis; single-author claim with no expert uptake.

events.what: Goldston/Lee/Schettler/Suriajaya papers (2503.15449, 2507.06823) and 2501.14545 use PCC as a hypothesis to derive consequences

judgement.doubts: Jerby's claim is also only RH-conditional; even if credible, whether that is 'whole' depends on reading the bullet as Montgomery's RH-framed conjecture. Set aside on F5 grounds, not on a found error; if a specialist later engages positively it should be revisited.

corrections.why: F5: the record itself says the claim of this significance sat 'unremarked for ten months', uncited, with the live Wikipedia article covering other 2025 developments in the same area but not this paper; full pair correlation even under RH is far beyond known methods. Several signals together make it not_credible, and no other event settles or bounds the bullet.
F5: with the only claim set aside, status is open and carries no direction.
